content:
Earlier in June this year, we highlighted three cases involving apps from Russian banks under U.S. sanctions bypassing review and appearing on the App Store. Two months later, another similar case has topped the iPhone App Store charts.

K8CHEN PRO is the latest such case. Its App Store listing disguises it as an augmented reality (AR)-driven kitchen design application.

Upon opening the app, the disguise almost immediately vanishes. The privacy policy linked from the App Store is noted as generated by "Free Privacy Policy Generator" — a potential red flag in itself.

Regardless, this app is unmistakably T-Bank's client application. What I find interesting is how such apps can repeatedly pass through the App Store review process.

When these apps get widely reported and climb the App Store rankings, it's plainly obvious that they should never have been there in the first place. This situation is troubling.

The other two cases mentioned in June can be found here and here.

Update: As expected, the app has already been removed from the App Store.
